From 25 July to 1 November 2026, the left wing galleries of the 2nd floor of the main building of the Latvian National Museum of Art in Riga (Jaņa Rozentāla laukums 1) host the exhibition *Contemporary Drawings: Florence and Daniel Guerlain’s Donation and Gifts to Centre Pompidou*.

This exhibition is an internationally significant and artistically highly valuable collaboration project between the Latvian National Museum of Art (LNMA) and Centre Pompidou. It presents works from the collection donated by collectors and art patrons Florence and Daniel Guerlain to the French institution over the past twenty years.

…

The exhibition is organised by the Latvian National Museum of Art and Centre Pompidou in Paris. The curator is Laetitia Pesenti, Curatorial Officer of the Graphic Arts Department at Centre Pompidou, and the project manager is Dr. art. Ginta Gerharde-Upeniece, Head of the Latvian Visual Arts Department at LNMA, with the participation of the donors, Florence and Daniel Guerlain.

In this year’s LNMA exhibition programme, drawing is highlighted as a vital artistic medium. From 18 July to 8 November, the Great Hall houses a large-scale Latvian drawings exhibition *Embodied Thought*. To showcase the global possibilities and trends of drawing techniques, the museum simultaneously presents contemporary drawings from Centre Pompidou, creating an indirect dialogue with the development of drawing in Latvian art.

…

Legacy]

From 16 September to 22 November 2026, the Museum of Decorative Arts and Design in Riga (Skārņu iela 10) hosts the exhibition *Rūdolfs Heimrāts 100. Legacy*, dedicated to the centenary of the outstanding textile artist Rūdolfs Heimrāts (1926–1992) who was professor at the Art Academy of Latvia and founder of the Latvian textile art school.

…

The exhibition unveils Rūdolfs Heimrāts’ multifaceted creative and pedagogical legacy, highlighting his significant contribution to the development of Latvian textile art in the second half of the 20th century. Alongside tapestries, decorative textiles, fabric print designs, and ceramics, special consideration is given to his work as an educator at the Art Academy of Latvia who has inspired several generations of textile artists. Visitors will enjoy exploring Heimrāts’ works from various museum collections, learn about the unrealised creative projects from his family archive, documentary films and photographs from private archives and the Latvian State Archives of Audiovisual Documents. The display also features vibrant fabric prints and innovative textile designs in different techniques. For the first time a particular focus has been placed on Heimrāts’ collaboration with architects (M. Staņa, Dz. Driba, O. Ostenbergs, L. A. Knāķe, M. Ģelzis, and others) and his contribution to the development of interior design.

…

From 18 July to 8 November 2026, the Great Hall of the main building of Latvian National Museum of Art in Riga (Jaņa Rozentāla laukums 1) will host the major exhibition of drawings, *Embodied Thought*. This is the first overview of such a scale in Latvia dedicated exclusively to drawing, which will reveal the diversity of the medium tracing its historical development in Latvia from the 18th to the 21st century.

…

The exposition brings together authors from different generations for whom drawing has played a significant role in their practice. Beginning with Johann Christoph Brotze, continuing through the classics of Latvian art and contemporary artists, and concluding with artists born in the 1990s, the exhibition also includes works created in exile and within the Latvian diaspora. In total, it features 97 personalities and more than 300 works.

…

The exhibition features works from the collections of Latvian National Museum of Art, Art Academy of Latvia, Latvian National Museum of History, Academic Library of the University of Latvia, the art collection of the liquidating ABLV Bank, the Madona Museum of Local History and Art, Tukums Museum, Zuzeum Art Museum, Latvian Centre for Contemporary Art, VV Foundation, Centre Pompidou National Museum of Modern Art in Paris, as well as private collections, including those of artists. It also presents newly commissioned works by three emerging authors: Marta Folkmane, Anna Malicka and Luīze Rukšāne."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://lnmm.gov.lv/en/latvian-national-museum-of-art/exhibitions/dreams-of-various-length-569","title":"Dreams of Various Length - Art Museums","description":"From 14 February to 16 August 2026, as part of The Generation cycle, the exhibition Dreams of Various Length is on view in the right wing galleries of the 2nd floor of the main building of the Latvian National Museum of Art in Riga (Jaņa Rozentāla ...","relevance":"high","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[Dreams of Various Length]

From 14 February to 16 August 2026, as part of *The Generation* cycle, the exhibition *Dreams of Various Length* is on view in the right wing galleries of the 2nd floor of the main building of the Latvian National Museum of Art in Riga (Jaņa Rozentāla laukums 1) revealing manifestations of Surrealism in Latvian printmaking during the 1970s and 1980s.

The exhibition focuses on interpretations of Surrealism in the oeuvre of eight graphic artists – Māris Ārgalis (1954–2008), Ilmārs Blumbergs (1943–2016), Valija Brence (1941–2009), Maija Dragūne (1945), Arthur Nikitin (1936–2022), Aija Ozoliņa (1932–2023), Māra Rikmane (1939), and Lolita Zikmane (1941). results.description: From 25 July to 1 November 2026, the left wing galleries of the 2nd floor of the main building of the Latvian National Museum of Art in Riga (Jaņa Rozentāla laukums 1) host the exhibition Contemporary Drawings: Florence and Daniel Guerlain’s Donation and Gifts to Centre Pompidou.

highlights:
[Contemporary Drawings]

From 25 July to 1 November 2026, the left wing galleries of the 2nd floor of the main building of the Latvian National Museum of Art in Riga (Jaņa Rozentāla laukums 1) host the exhibition *Contemporary Drawings: Florence and Daniel Guerlain’s Donation and Gifts to Centre Pompidou*.

This exhibition is an internationally significant and artistically highly valuable collaboration project between the Latvian National Museum of Art (LNMA) and Centre Pompidou. It presents works from the collection donated by collectors and art patrons Florence and Daniel Guerlain to the French institution over the past twenty years.

…

The exhibition is organised by the Latvian National Museum of Art and Centre Pompidou in Paris. The curator is Laetitia Pesenti, Curatorial Officer of the Graphic Arts Department at Centre Pompidou, and the project manager is Dr. art. Ginta Gerharde-Upeniece, Head of the Latvian Visual Arts Department at LNMA, with the participation of the donors, Florence and Daniel Guerlain.

In this year’s LNMA exhibition programme, drawing is highlighted as a vital artistic medium. From 18 July to 8 November, the Great Hall houses a large-scale Latvian drawings exhibition *Embodied Thought*. To showcase the global possibilities and trends of drawing techniques, the museum simultaneously presents contemporary drawings from Centre Pompidou, creating an indirect dialogue with the development of drawing in Latvian art.

results.title: Rūdolfs Heimrāts 100. Legacy - Art Museums
results.description: From 16 September to 22 November 2026, the Museum of Decorative Arts and Design in Riga (Skārņu iela 10) hosts the exhibition Rūdolfs Heimrāts 100.

highlights:
[Rūdolfs Heimrāts 100. Legacy]

From 16 September to 22 November 2026, the Museum of Decorative Arts and Design in Riga (Skārņu iela 10) hosts the exhibition *Rūdolfs Heimrāts 100. Legacy*, dedicated to the centenary of the outstanding textile artist Rūdolfs Heimrāts (1926–1992) who was professor at the Art Academy of Latvia and founder of the Latvian textile art school.

…

The exhibition unveils Rūdolfs Heimrāts’ multifaceted creative and pedagogical legacy, highlighting his significant contribution to the development of Latvian textile art in the second half of the 20th century. Alongside tapestries, decorative textiles, fabric print designs, and ceramics, special consideration is given to his work as an educator at the Art Academy of Latvia who has inspired several generations of textile artists. Visitors will enjoy exploring Heimrāts’ works from various museum collections, learn about the unrealised creative projects from his family archive, documentary films and photographs from private archives and the Latvian State Archives of Audiovisual Documents. The display also features vibrant fabric prints and innovative textile designs in different techniques. For the first time a particular focus has been placed on Heimrāts’ collaboration with architects (M. Staņa, Dz. Driba, O. Ostenbergs, L. A. Knāķe, M. Ģelzis, and others) and his contribution to the development of interior design.

results.title: Embodied Thought - Art Museums
results.description: From 18 July to 8 November 2026, the Great Hall of the main building of Latvian National Museum of Art in Riga (Jaņa Rozentāla laukums 1) will host the major exhibition of drawings, Embodied Thought.

highlights:
[Embodied Thought]

From 18 July to 8 November 2026, the Great Hall of the main building of Latvian National Museum of Art in Riga (Jaņa Rozentāla laukums 1) will host the major exhibition of drawings, *Embodied Thought*. This is the first overview of such a scale in Latvia dedicated exclusively to drawing, which will reveal the diversity of the medium tracing its historical development in Latvia from the 18th to the 21st century.

…

The exposition brings together authors from different generations for whom drawing has played a significant role in their practice. Beginning with Johann Christoph Brotze, continuing through the classics of Latvian art and contemporary artists, and concluding with artists born in the 1990s, the exhibition also includes works created in exile and within the Latvian diaspora. In total, it features 97 personalities and more than 300 works.

…

The exhibition features works from the collections of Latvian National Museum of Art, Art Academy of Latvia, Latvian National Museum of History, Academic Library of the University of Latvia, the art collection of the liquidating ABLV Bank, the Madona Museum of Local History and Art, Tukums Museum, Zuzeum Art Museum, Latvian Centre for Contemporary Art, VV Foundation, Centre Pompidou National Museum of Modern Art in Paris, as well as private collections, including those of artists. It also presents newly commissioned works by three emerging authors: Marta Folkmane, Anna Malicka and Luīze Rukšāne.

results.title: Dreams of Various Length - Art Museums
results.description: From 14 February to 16 August 2026, as part of The Generation cycle, the exhibition Dreams of Various Length is on view in the right wing galleries of the 2nd floor of the main building of the Latvian National Museum of Art in Riga (Jaņa Rozentāla ...

highlights:
[Dreams of Various Length]

From 14 February to 16 August 2026, as part of *The Generation* cycle, the exhibition *Dreams of Various Length* is on view in the right wing galleries of the 2nd floor of the main building of the Latvian National Museum of Art in Riga (Jaņa Rozentāla laukums 1) revealing manifestations of Surrealism in Latvian printmaking during the 1970s and 1980s.

The exhibition focuses on interpretations of Surrealism in the oeuvre of eight graphic artists – Māris Ārgalis (1954–2008), Ilmārs Blumbergs (1943–2016), Valija Brence (1941–2009), Maija Dragūne (1945), Arthur Nikitin (1936–2022), Aija Ozoliņa (1932–2023), Māra Rikmane (1939), and Lolita Zikmane (1941). Currently not equally known and studied, these talented authors worked under Soviet occupation in the 1970s and 80s, when Surrealism, alongside Abstractionism, was placed on the list of art directions undesirable to Soviet ideology.

From 30 May to 23 August 2026, the Museum of Decorative Arts and Design will host the exhibition *In the Name of Clay: 50 Years of Italian Ceramic Art*, tracing the development of Italian contemporary ceramics from the post-war period to the present day.

…

The exhibition at the Museum of Decorative Arts and Design is part of the Latvia Ceramics Biennale’s interseason programme and is organized in co-operation with the Latvian Centre for Contemporary Ceramics and the International Museum of Ceramics in Faenza.
